about.label: Degree pathway
about.text: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Economics & Finance (Liberal)

blocks.text: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyses, and interprets data to help organisations make better decisions. Data analysts turn raw information into reports, dashboards, trends, and actionable recommendations.
A background in Economics & Finance can be especially useful for analysing revenue, costs, consumer behaviour, market trends, financial performance, pricing, and business growth.
Students following this pathway should combine their understanding of economics and finance with practical skills in statistics, Excel, SQL, data visualisation, and Python.
Who is this career suited for?

items.text: Students who enjoy working with numbers, patterns, and evidence.
Students interested in business performance, markets, banking, or finance.
Students who like solving problems and explaining findings clearly.
Students who want a career that can lead to business intelligence, financial analytics, or data science.

sections.heading: What does a Data Analyst do?

blocks.text: Collect and prepare data
Gather data from spreadsheets, databases, business systems, surveys, and financial records; clean errors and handle missing values.
Analyse trends and patterns
Use statistics, comparisons, segmentation, and exploratory analysis to understand what is happening and why it may be happening.
Create dashboards and reports
Present KPIs, financial trends, customer metrics, and operational performance through clear visualisations.
Support business decisions
Explain findings, identify opportunities or risks, and recommend actions grounded in evidence.
Financial Data Analytics
Analyse revenue, expenses, budgets, profitability, financial performance, and business forecasts.
Business Intelligence (BI)
Build dashboards, track business KPIs, monitor operational performance, and support management decisions.
Customer & Marketing Analytics
Study customer segments, sales patterns, campaign performance, retention, and purchasing behaviour.
Economic & Market Research Analytics
Analyse inflation, employment, demand, pricing, industry trends, and economic indicators.
Risk & Operations Analytics
Explore operational efficiency, credit-related data, process bottlenecks, and risk indicators within the limits of the role.
Recommended undergraduate pathway

A BA, BSc, or interdisciplinary Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies degree with a focus on Economics & Finance can provide a useful foundation for data analytics. Exact degree titles, quantitative coursework, and eligibility requirements vary by institution.

rows.text: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, financial literacy, mathematics, introductory statistics
Econometrics, quantitative research, financial accounting, spreadsheets, data interpretation
SQL, data visualisation, business analytics, Python, applied statistics
Advanced analytics, forecasting, research dissertation, internship or capstone

blocks.label: Useful electives or minors
blocks.text: Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Business Analytics, Accounting, or Information Systems.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Some data analyst vacancies require a degree with substantial quantitative coursework. If your programme has limited mathematics or statistics, strengthen your profile through electives and practical projects. For more technical analytics roles, advanced statistics, programming, or postgraduate study may be helpful.
Year 1
Build the quantitative foundation

items.text: Study microeconomics, macroeconomics, and basic accounting.
Learn Excel formulas, sorting, filtering, charts, and pivot tables.
Understand averages, percentages, distributions, and basic probability.
Practise interpreting tables, charts, and economic indicators.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Analyse a small sales or economic dataset in Excel and write a short findings report.
Year 2
Learn statistics and data querying

items.text: Study regression, hypothesis testing, sampling, and econometrics.

blocks.label: Learn SQL
blocks.text: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOIN, and aggregate functions.

items.text: Practise data cleaning, validation, and exploratory analysis.
Learn financial statements, profitability ratios, and budget variance analysis.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Use SQL or spreadsheets to answer a set of business questions using a structured dataset.
Year 3
Develop analytics and visualisation skills

items.text: Learn Power BI or Tableau, including data modelling and dashboard design.
Learn Python with pandas, NumPy, and matplotlib.
Practise business KPI analysis, customer segmentation, and trend analysis.
Apply for data analytics, finance analytics, or business intelligence internships.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Complete two portfolio projects and explain how the results inform decisions.
Year 4, if applicable
Prepare for employment

items.text: Complete an internship, supervised research project, or capstone.
Strengthen SQL, dashboard storytelling, and statistical reasoning.
Practise business case studies and data interpretation interviews.
Prepare a resume and portfolio tailored to analyst job descriptions.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Present three or more well-documented projects and apply for suitable entry-level positions.

rows.text: Data cleaning, calculations, pivot tables, reporting
Querying and combining data from databases
Data preparation, analysis, and repeatable workflows
Regression and analysis of economic relationships
Budgets, revenue analysis, and financial performance
Version control and reproducible analytical work

blocks.label: Recommended learning order
blocks.text: Excel → statistics → SQL → Power BI → Python. Start applying for internships once you can analyse a dataset and communicate your findings; you do not need to master every tool first.
Aim to complete at least three projects. Use public, synthetic, or appropriately authorised datasets, and clearly distinguish measured results from estimates.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Sales & Profitability Dashboard
Beginner

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: An Excel or Power BI dashboard that tracks sales, revenue, costs, profit margins, and monthly trends.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Data cleaning, KPI calculation, comparisons, and dashboard design.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A dashboard and a short report recommending areas for further investigation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Economic Indicators Analysis
Beginner–Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Analyse selected economic indicators, such as inflation, GDP growth, employment, or interest rates, over time.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Time-series visualisation, data validation, comparisons, and interpretation of economic context.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A notebook or report explaining trends, limitations, and possible relationships without claiming causation from correlation alone.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: SQL Business Analysis
Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Use a sample retail or transaction database to answer questions about revenue, product performance, customer segments, and repeat purchases.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: SQL joins, aggregation, filtering, data quality checks, and business interpretation.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A set of documented queries and a concise findings report.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Personal Finance or Budget Variance Analysis
Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Compare budgeted and actual expenses or analyse a fictional company's financial performance.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Variance analysis, category-level comparisons, trend detection, and clear reporting.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A dashboard with explanations for material differences and recommendations for further review.

blocks.label: Portfolio tip
blocks.text: Every project should answer six questions: What was the problem? Where did the data come from? How was it cleaned? Which methods were used? What did the analysis reveal? What action could the findings support?
Search for related job titles because employers may advertise entry-level analytics positions under different names.

rows.text: Regular reporting, spreadsheet automation, data validation

blocks.text: Potential employers and work environments include:

blocks.label: IT and analytics consulting
blocks.text: Accenture, Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and analytics service providers.

blocks.label: Financial services
blocks.text: Banks, insurance companies, fintech businesses, and financial services firms.

blocks.label: Technology and e-commerce
blocks.text: SaaS businesses, retail platforms, and technology companies with analytics teams.

blocks.label: Research and economic analysis
blocks.text: Research consultancies, market research firms, policy organisations, and economic research groups.

blocks.label: Corporate analytics teams
blocks.text: Manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, consumer goods, and other organisations that use business data.

These are examples to investigate, not confirmed current vacancies. Some finance-related roles require additional accounting, financial modelling, or domain knowledge. Check each vacancy's eligibility criteria.
Focus on practical learning that supports your portfolio.

rows.text: Pivot tables, lookup functions, data cleaning, Power Query
Queries, joins, grouping, subqueries, and window functions
Data modelling, Power Query, DAX fundamentals, dashboard design
pandas, NumPy, visualisation, exploratory data analysis
Financial statements, budgeting, profitability, variance analysis
Econometrics, time-series analysis, interpreting economic indicators

blocks.text: Potential learning sources include Microsoft Learn, introductory SQL courses, university statistics and econometrics courses, and established data analytics training providers. Verify the current curriculum, costs, and certification conditions before enrolling.

blocks.label: Certification strategy
blocks.text: Start with one structured data analytics course, then build a project using the skills learned. A strong portfolio and sound analytical reasoning can be more useful than collecting numerous certificates without practical experience.
Undergraduate degree
Economics & Finance + statistics and quantitative skills
Data / Research / Reporting Intern
Build foundational analytical experience
Junior Data Analyst / Data Analyst
Own datasets, reports, queries, and dashboards
Senior Data Analyst / Business Intelligence Analyst
Lead analytical projects and advise stakeholders
Analytics Lead / Analytics Manager
Guide analytical strategy, delivery, and teams

Other potential directions include financial analytics, economic research, product analytics, business intelligence, risk analytics, and data science. Moving into data science or specialised quantitative finance may require deeper mathematics, programming, and sometimes postgraduate study.
These are broad planning estimates, not verified current salary quotations or guaranteed offers. Actual compensation depends on location, employer, technical skills, domain expertise, and experience.

rows.text: Stipend varies widely; some internships are unpaid

blocks.text: These ranges are indicative only. Some reporting roles may pay less, while specialised analytics positions at larger employers may pay more. Finance-domain expertise can be an advantage, but it does not guarantee a higher salary.
Analytical thinking
Break down business questions and identify useful patterns in data.
Quantitative reasoning
Understand statistics, percentages, distributions, and basic regression.
Technical proficiency
Use Excel, SQL, and a visualisation tool to analyse data.
Business and financial understanding
Connect results to revenue, costs, profitability, markets, and organisational objectives.
Communication
Explain findings and recommendations clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
Data quality and ethics
Validate data, protect sensitive information, and avoid misleading conclusions.
Problem-solving
Translate an unclear business problem into measurable questions and an analytical approach.

By graduation, a well-prepared student should aim to have:

items.text: A foundation in economics, finance, statistics, and quantitative reasoning.
Practical proficiency in Excel, SQL, and Power BI or Tableau.
Working knowledge of Python for data cleaning and analysis.
Three or more documented projects using business, financial, or economic datasets.
Experience through an internship, research project, or practical assignment.
The ability to explain findings, limitations, and recommendations to business stakeholders.
Awareness of data privacy, data quality, and responsible interpretation.

blocks.text: Final recommendation
The Economics & Finance → Data Analyst pathway is a practical choice for students who want to combine business understanding with analytical problem-solving.

The student's strongest differentiator will be the ability to do more than produce charts: they should understand the business or economic question, analyse the data accurately, and explain what decision the evidence can reasonably support.
